title: Per-token stage scanfield notes: e2e latency splits and trace sketches
body:
Purpose:
Quick field notes from an ad-hoc investigation into per-token, per-stage latency characteristics observed in production traces for route /v1/generate (rev: 2026-01-29). Goal: surface dominant per-stage contributors at p50/p95/p99, sketch hypotheses for long tails, and list next experiments.

Summary findings (top-line):
- p50 dominated by model forward compute (emit stage) plus ~2ms tokenization/warmup overhead.
- p95 shows significant amplification from async-batcher wait time and KV-store miss penalties (KV miss ~12ms extra on p95).
- p99 dominated by two orthogonal causes: cold KV cache (miss + refill, often compounded with batch eviction) and intermittent spike in egress/transit when responses cross a specific proxy (proxy->egress hop adds 30-80ms).
- Observed correlation between sequence length and batch wait: longer prompts increase batch queue time non-linearly for adaptive batching policy.

Data snapshot (sample window: 2026-02-01 00:00 -> 2026-02-07 23:59, N=45k traces):
- p50: 42ms
- p95: 162ms
- p99: 502ms
- median emit-stage token time (per-token on A100-type node): 18ms
- batch-wait median: 6ms, p95 batch-wait: 88ms, p99 batch-wait: 390ms
- KV cache hit rate on sample cohort: 88% overall; for cold-start subset (~6% of requests) hit rate 22%

Trace anatomy (canonical stage list):
1) ingress (edge TLS + routing): 2-6ms typical, spikes to 25ms when region failover occurs
2) tokenization: 1-4ms, deterministic by tokenizer type
3) route-routing & auth checks: 1-3ms
4) batching/queue (adaptive batcher): highly variable, 0-400ms
5) KV cache lookup (prefix/KV store): 0-120ms (miss + refill penalty >100ms in worst cases)
6) model forward (emit stage): 10-60ms depending on sequence step and quantization profile
7) postprocess/format + egress: 1-80ms (proxy-related spikes observed)

Key trace patterns discovered:
- Pattern A (common p95 slice): small prompt, single-token emit, batch-wait ~70-120ms, KV hit: yes, model emit fast -> tail from batcher scheduling window.
- Pattern B (p99 heavy): medium prompt, long prefix, KV miss triggered mid-response causing synchronous refill while batcher still holding other requests -> cascading delay (KV miss adds ~110-180ms).
- Pattern C (sporadic p99): small prompt but egress hop across proxy X (NOT the usual regional egress) which adds ~40-80ms; often correlated with node scaling events and stale route mappings.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Adaptive batcher configuration has a pathological regime for low QPS + variable seqlen: batching triggers wait windows that inflate p95/p99.
2) KV store eviction policy + refill path is not optimized for mid-request refills (sync IO blocking model thread).
3) Egress/proxy path occasionally routes through suboptimal hop during ASG churn; route-level sticky mapping fails to update quickly.
4) High quantization/compilation fallbacks (when device runs out of fav kernels) can temporarily increase model forward time by 1.5x-2x.

Evidence and quick checks performed: 
- Correlation matrix (trace tags): batch-wait vs seqlen shows Pearson r=+0.41, stronger for QPS<2 (r=+0.63).
- KV miss traces: 2/3 of p99 traces show KV miss; TTL + eviction trace IDs point to frequent small-key churn in prefix cache.
- Instance-level logs: during several p99 windows, node reported high slab-eviction events right before affected traces.
- Network hop analysis: using tcpdump/hops, we saw 3 cases where egress used proxy-beta rather than proxy-stable — all coincident with k8s node drain + new ENI attach.

Immediate mitigations attempted (results):
- Reduced adaptive batcher max-wait from 50ms -> 20ms in canary region: p95 improved ~9% for canary route; p99 improved ~5% but too noisy to be definitive.
- Switched KV refill to background async prefetch for canary traces with predictable prefixes: KV miss penalty on that cohort dropped from median 120ms -> 10ms (good signal).
- Temporary egress route pinning for a subset of flows prevented proxy-bounce; observed elimination of proxy-related spikes in that cohort.

Action items (next experiments):
- Experiment 1: Canary adaptive-batcher: new policy using seqlen-weighted batching (weight short seq less) for 24h and measure p50/p95/p99 by seqlen cohort.
- Experiment 2: KV store: instrument separate async refill path and disable sync refill on hot path; run A/B to measure p95 delta.
- Experiment 3: Egress healthcheck + sticky-routing: rollout sticky routing on node attach events for 48h to catch proxy bounce.
- Experiment 4: Kernel/quantization hot-swap metric: add telemetry to record kernel fallback counts per request and correlate to model-forward durations.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How much of p99 remains unexplained after batcher + KV async fixes? We should allocate a 1-week window for triage after both changes land.
- Are there any SLOs that need immediate customer comms? Current SLA impact minimal but p99 regressions are visible to a small set of high-traffic tenants. Recommend reaching out to affected customers post-mitigation with technical summary.

Quick check commands used (notes):
- trace sample pull: ./tools/trace-query --route /v1/generate --from 2026-02-03 --to 2026-02-05 --quantiles p50,p95,p99 --stages all --out sample.json
- kv hit extraction: jq '.traces[] | select(.kv_hit==false) | {id: .id, ts: .ts, stage_times: .stage_times}' sample.json | wc -l
- batcher logs tail: kubectl logs -n serving adaptive-batcher-*/ -c batcher | grep 'wait_ms' | tail -n 200

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight; aim is to capture field intuition and next steps so SRE and runtime teams can prioritize.
- Marcus will take lead on Experiment 1; Priya on Experiment 2; Liam on Experiment 3.

Appendix (trace exemplar):
- exemplar trace id: T-20260203-7a9f (p99)
  timeline: ingress 3ms -> tokenizer 1ms -> route 2ms -> batch_wait 312ms -> kv_lookup 118ms (miss) -> model_emit 24ms -> postproc 5ms -> egress 8ms = total 473ms

Todo / backlog notes:
- Add synthetic microbench harness that can replay KV misses in isolation and measure impact on local model threads (ranked high).
- Add billing tag to traces so we can target tenants impacted by p99 earlier.
- Draft short postmortem template for long-tail latency spikes (link to JIRA-RT-4923).

End of notes.
